A 64-year-old woman with a 10-year history of diabetes mellitus presents with fever and cough lasting
five days. She has been using over-the-counter medications for three days without significant
improvement. Her vital signs include a pulse of 72 beats/min (regular), blood pressure of 151/85
mmHg, respiratory rate of 17 breaths/min, and a temperature of 101ºF. Physical examination reveals
no abnormalities. Initial laboratory findings are as follows: Hemoglobin: 10.9 g/dL Leukocytes:
12,000/mm³ Platelet count: 159,000/mm³ Random Blood Sugar: 189 mg/dL Blood Urea Nitrogen: 19
mg/dL Serum Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL Serum Sodium: 142 mEq/L Serum Potassium: 4.3 mEq/L Serum
Calcium: 8.9 mg/dL Serum Magnesium: 1.6 mEq/L Serum Bicarbonate: 21 mEq/L Serum Cholesterol:
245 mg/dL HbA1c: 8.9% (<6%). The patient is prescribed antibiotics for one week. By the fourth day,
her fever resolves, but on the sixth day, she returns with severe burning during urination. Examination
shows she is afebrile, hemodynamically stable, but has tenderness in the pubic region. Repeat
laboratory tests reveal: Hemoglobin: 10.7 g/dL Leukocytes: 8,000/mm³ Platelet count: 179,000/mm³
Random Blood Sugar: 201 mg/dL Blood Urea Nitrogen: 20 mg/dL Serum Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL
